name: Tessier Number 6 Facial Cleft

criteria.description: Presence of a lateral facial cleft extending from the oral commissure towards the temporal region
Involvement of the lateral orbital rim or lateral canthus with soft tissue and bony defects
Unilateral or bilateral macrostomia (enlarged mouth aperture) associated with the cleft
Hypoplasia or absence of the zygomatic bone on the affected side

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a lateral facial cleft extending from the oral commissure with involvement of the lateral orbital rim or zygomatic bone defect
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging to assess bony involvement

pathognomonic.symptomName: Lateral facial cleft extending from oral commissure to temporal region
searchTerms: side of face cleft from mouth to temple

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hypoplasia or absence of zygomatic bone

common.symptomName: Soft tissue deficiency along the cleft margin
searchTerms: missing soft tissue near facial cleft
skin and muscle gap along cleft
soft tissue loss at cleft edge

common.symptomName: Difficulty with oral competence and feeding

occasional.symptomName: Conductive hearing loss due to external auditory canal involvement
searchTerms: hearing loss from ear canal blockage
conductive deafness due to ear canal

rare.symptomName: Cleft palate associated with lateral facial cleft
searchTerms: split roof of mouth with facial cleft
opening in palate with cheek cleft

imaging: CT scan showing bony defects of the zygomatic arch and lateral orbital rim
MRI to evaluate soft tissue involvement and intracranial anomalies
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; sporadic occurrence predominates
other: Clinical examination revealing lateral facial cleft and macrostomia

distinguishingFeatures: Cleft extends more posteriorly towards the ear
Involvement of the mandibular ramus rather than zygomatic bone
Presence of epibulbar dermoids and vertebral anomalies

redFlags: Severe feeding difficulties leading to failure to thrive
Respiratory distress due to airway obstruction
Signs of intracranial involvement or neurological deficits
references: Tessier P. Anatomical classification of facial clefts. J Maxillofac Surg. 1976.
Orphanet: Tessier number 6 facial cleft - ORPHA:141265
Mulliken JB, et al. Craniofacial clefts: a review. Plast Reconstr Surg. 1985.
